themes_detail.label: Sanitation Infrastructure Collapse
themes_detail.summary: This week, the Upper East Side is experiencing a cascading sanitation crisis with litter baskets (627% spike), dumpsters (967% spike), and commercial disposal complaints (500% spike) all surging simultaneously—10 litter basket requests this week vs. 1.4 weekly average, 4 dumpster complaints this week vs. 0.4 average—suggesting either sudden infrastructure failures or a major service gap in waste management.
evidence: Litter Basket Request: 10 complaints THIS WEEK vs 1.4 weekly average (627% spike, z-score 17.82)
Dumpster Complaint: 4 complaints THIS WEEK vs 0.4 weekly average (967% spike, z-score 7.49)
Litter Basket Complaint: 4 complaints THIS WEEK vs 0.5 weekly average (700% spike, z-score 7.0)
Commercial Disposal Complaint: 3 complaints THIS WEEK vs 0.5 weekly average (500% spike, z-score 3.54)
reporting_angles: Interview Sanitation Department about whether this week saw staffing shortages, equipment failures, or route changes
Canvass blocks with highest spike complaints to document visible conditions and resident frustration
Cross-reference with any recent privatization or contractor changes in waste collection

themes_detail.label: Tree Infrastructure Degradation
themes_detail.summary: Over the past week, dead or dying tree complaints have surged 1500% (4 complaints last week vs 0.2 weekly average, z-score 8.66), signaling either sudden disease outbreak, storm damage, or deferred maintenance in the district's urban forest.
evidence: Dead/Dying Tree complaints: 4 complaints last week vs 0.2 weekly average (1500% spike, z-score 8.66)
Spike began within last 2 weeks, indicating rapid onset rather than chronic neglect
High z-score (8.66) indicates statistically rare event in district baseline
reporting_angles: Investigate whether recent storm, pest infestation, or drought conditions triggered die-off
Interview Parks Department about maintenance schedules and tree health assessments
Map locations of 311 complaints to identify hotspots and visual pattern of damage

themes_detail.label: Leash Law Enforcement Breakdown
themes_detail.summary: This week, unleashed dog complaints jumped 700% (3 complaints this week vs 0.4 weekly average, z-score 5.42), suggesting either a sudden surge in off-leash violations or a breakdown in Animal Care and Control enforcement in the district.
evidence: Unleashed Dog complaints: 3 complaints THIS WEEK vs 0.4 weekly average (700% spike, z-score 5.42)
Spike is concurrent with litter and dumpster spikes, suggesting possible district-wide service degradation
High z-score indicates anomalous behavior for this district baseline
reporting_angles: Contact NYC Parks Enforcement and Animal Care & Control about staffing or patrol changes this week
Interview residents at parks where complaints originated about safety concerns
Determine if spike correlates with specific parks or broader neighborhood pattern

themes_detail.label: Street Furniture Damage Wave
themes_detail.summary: Three weeks ago, street sign damage complaints spiked 567% (10 complaints vs 1.5 weekly average, z-score 7.6), indicating either vandalism, poor maintenance, or accident damage affecting the district's infrastructure signage.
evidence: Street Sign - Damaged: 10 complaints 3 weeks ago vs 1.5 weekly average (567% spike, z-score 7.6)
Timing is 3 weeks prior, making this lower priority than THIS WEEK spikes
May indicate ongoing maintenance backlog if complaints persist
reporting_angles: Request Department of Transportation data on sign replacement rates and damage causes
Verify whether damage spike correlates with specific incident (accident, storm, vandalism surge)

themes_detail.label: Childcare Regulation Violations
themes_detail.summary: This week, day care complaints surged 500% (3 complaints this week vs 0.5 weekly average, z-score 5.0), suggesting possible unlicensed operations, safety violations, or enforcement actions in the district's childcare sector.
evidence: Day Care complaints: 3 complaints THIS WEEK vs 0.5 weekly average (500% spike, z-score 5.0)
Spike is acute and recent, requiring investigation into cause
No context available on complaint types (licensing, safety, conditions, etc.)
reporting_angles: Request 311 complaint details to understand nature of violations (licensing, safety, health code)
Cross-reference with NYC Department of Health and Mental Hygiene enforcement actions this week
Interview parents or facilities about what prompted reports
